## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Sanidassanattika, Savicāraduka* (Patthana 16.83) is an Abhidhamma text belonging to the *Paṭṭhāna* collection [SuttaCentral]. It forms a sub-section within the *Paṭṭhāna* analytical framework, treating conditional relations across the combination of the triad of visible phenomena (*sanidassanattika*) and the dyad associated with sustained thought or examination (*savicāraduka*) [SuttaCentral].
Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus identifies any cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus reveals widespread formulaic repetition across the Abhidhamma, identifying 158 matching passages shared across 50 different Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest textual overlaps occur with other sections of the *Paṭṭhāna*, particularly the *Sanidassanasappaṭighattika* (Patthana 1.23; 15 matches, 3,287 shared characters) and the *Tika Hetuduka* (Patthana 4.1; 10 matches, 2,255 shared characters) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, substantial reuse is found across structurally related triad-dyad pairs, including *Sanidassanattika, Āsavaduka* (Patthana 16.58), *Sanidassanattika, Kusalattika* (Patthana 17.27), *Sanidassanattika, Sāsavaduka* (Patthana 16.59), and the closely adjacent *Sanidassanattika, Savitakkaduka* (Patthana 16.82) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
